FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} spread in a thin layer in a pan wider than it is deep, never stirred, with {1_coll} and {2_coll}. The gilded crust that catches on the bottom is called the socarrat, and it is fought over.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: toasted bread rubbed with raw {2_plur} and then with {1_plur} cut in half, until nothing but the skin is left. Salt, oil, nothing else — and yet a whole art is made of it in Barcelona.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} dipped three times into boiling water before it is left there — otherwise the skin comes away — cut with scissors over rounds of {1_adj}, oil and smoked paprika.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a {0_adj} dough pushed through a star nozzle straight into the oil — the flutes keep them from bursting — rolled in {1_plur} and dipped into thick {2_coll}.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: patatas bravas
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} in irregular cubes fried twice, drowned in a {1_adj} sauce and a {2_adj} emulsion. Speared on a toothpick, standing at the bar.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: romesco
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} toasted, {1_coll} roasted and dried {2_coll} ground in a mortar with fried bread that binds the whole. Eaten off sweet onions cooked under the ashes, straight from the hand.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} ground with crumb and mounted with oil into an orange cream thick enough to stand up, served iced with hard-boiled {2_coll} crumbled over. Denser than gazpacho, of which it is the Córdoban cousin.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: fideuà

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: migas
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: hard bread damped the day before, crumbled and fried at length in {1_adj} fat until it turns golden and loose, served with {2_plur}. A shepherd's lunch, made of what was left.
